correctness.rationale: For every x>=3 and r in {1,2}, fixed-length sums of a,a+1,a+2,a+3 form a complete integer interval, giving exact quotient intervals I_h. Nesting J_h and the first full set of x residues give exact Apéry representatives w(t). The two explicit staircase branches yield generators, Selmer formulas determine genus/Frobenius, and elementary generator-edge comparisons determine the maximal Apéry elements (hence pseudo-Frobenius set). The proof addresses endpoints x=3 and all residue cases. Standalone verify.py passed 1596 formula checks plus 176 direct exhaustive gap comparisons, which are additional, not infinite, evidence.

originality.rationale: The 2018 authors explicitly leave the 3-step finite arithmetic-progression quotient case with arbitrary denominator open. The 2023 almost-arithmetic progression quotient paper assumes the denominator divides the first generator; here the first generator is coprime to 3. A 2023 general quotient generator construction does not evaluate the present two-branch Apéry, Frobenius/genus, or pseudo-Frobenius formulas. 2026 GCNS quotient work assumes a different family and divisibility. Exact-source and semantic mathematical-record searches exposed no covering result, though a nonobvious implication of prior general formulas cannot be fully ruled out.

value.rationale: The 2018 arithmetic-progression quotient paper explicitly asks for genus/Frobenius calculations for finite progressions of length at least four and arbitrary denominator. For denominator 3 prime to its initial generator, this work gives closed quasi-polynomial Frobenius values, a simple exact genus law, and all pseudo-Frobenius elements including a structural type transition. The two-branch Apéry staircase is a reusable exact structural calculation; the infinite classification is materially more informative than routine individual numerical tests.
